info.text: Unit 20 — Simulation: building a full documentation trail. CEFR B2. Split by skill: Listening, Reading, Use of English, Vocabulary.

name.text: U20-L1 Dialogue 1 — where the fault is recorded

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again (Laying out the documentation trail). Where do you record the fault first?

generalfeedback.text: The mentor says: "You write the defect in the tech log, because every fault starts there." The tech log is always the first record.

feedback.text: Correct — every fault starts in the tech log.
The task card lists the repair steps; it does not record the original fault.
The store handles parts, not the defect record.

name.text: U20-L2 Dialogue 1 — where the repair steps live

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. True or false: the repair steps are in the IPC.

generalfeedback.text: False. "No. The repair steps are in the AMM, the aircraft maintenance manual." The IPC only holds the part numbers.

feedback.text: The IPC holds part numbers, not repair steps.
Correct — the repair steps are in the AMM.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again (Adding traceability to the parts). The seal came in a sealed bag with no serial number. Which number does the technician record?

generalfeedback.text: "Then record the batch number, since the seal has no serial number." A part with no serial number is traced by its batch number.

feedback.text: Correct — no serial number, so the batch number gives traceability.
There is no serial number on this seal.
That is not a part-traceability number.

name.text: U20-L4 Dialogue 3 — how many sign-off blocks

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again (Defending the trail to the auditor). How many sign-off blocks does the auditor see? Write the number.

generalfeedback.text: Two. "I can see two sign-off blocks." One is for the work, and the other is for the inspection.

feedback.text: Correct — two sign-off blocks: one for the work, one for the inspection.

name.text: U20-L5 Dialogue 3 — who is speaker A

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. True or false: speaker A is the auditor.

generalfeedback.text: True. A opens with "I am the auditor today. Show me the documentation trail for this defect."

feedback.text: Correct — A says "I am the auditor today."
Listen again to the first line: A introduces the auditor role.

name.text: U20-L6 Dialogue 2 — what confirms safety-critical work

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. What confirms the safety-critical work before release?

generalfeedback.text: "A dual inspection means a second person confirms the safety-critical work." A second qualified person must check it.

feedback.text: Correct — a second qualified person confirms it.
Safety-critical work needs a second person, not one signature alone.
A glance is not a recorded dual inspection.

name.text: U20-L7 Dialogue 1 — how many defects today

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. For how many defects do you build the documentation trail on simulation day? Write the number.

generalfeedback.text: One. "You must build a full documentation trail for one defect." The whole trail follows that single fault.

feedback.text: Correct — one defect, one clear trail, from find to fix.

questiontext.text:
Read the MEL entry.

MEL entry: The No. 2 cabin reading light is inoperative. Under the Minimum Equipment List, the aircraft may be dispatched with this item deferred for up to 10 days, provided the light is placarded 'INOP' and a repair interval is opened.

What does the MEL allow here?

generalfeedback.text: The Minimum Equipment List lets an aircraft fly with a listed item deferred, under conditions (here: a placard and a repair interval). It does not force grounding.

feedback.text: Correct — dispatch is allowed for up to 10 days under the stated conditions.
The MEL exists precisely to avoid grounding for a listed, deferrable item.

answer.text: Repair before the next flight only

feedback.text: The repair interval is up to 10 days, not before the next flight.

name.text: U20-R2 Service Bulletin — mandatory or not

questiontext.text:
Read the Service Bulletin note.

Service Bulletin SB-52-0042 (recommended) introduces an improved cabin door seal with a longer service life. It is not mandatory. Operators may embody it at the next scheduled door maintenance.

True or false: this Service Bulletin must be embodied before the next flight.

generalfeedback.text: False. The SB is marked "recommended" and "not mandatory"; it may be embodied at the next scheduled door maintenance.

feedback.text: A recommended SB is not compulsory before flight.
Correct — it is recommended, not mandatory.

questiontext.text:
Read the work-order note.

Work order WO-5501 was raised to investigate a repeated 'DOOR' caution on the flight deck. The tech log shows the same message on three sectors. The task card asks the technician to run a BITE test on the door control unit.

Why was the work order raised?

generalfeedback.text: The trigger was a recurring caution message ("the same message on three sectors"), so the job is to investigate it with a BITE test.

feedback.text: Correct — the same 'DOOR' caution appeared on three sectors.

answer.text: The door seal was worn on the edge

feedback.text: That is a different defect; this work order is about a caution message.
This is a fault investigation, not a scheduled overhaul.

questiontext.text:
Read the BITE readout.

BITE readout: DOOR CTRL UNIT — FAULT CODE 21-51, micro-switch open circuit. The built-in test equipment isolates the fault to the door micro-switch wiring, so the technician can go straight to the wiring diagram.

True or false: the BITE readout points the technician to the wiring diagram.

generalfeedback.text: True. The built-in test equipment isolates the fault to the micro-switch wiring, so the next document is the wiring diagram.

feedback.text: Correct — the readout sends the technician to the wiring diagram.
Read again: the fault is isolated to the wiring, so the wiring diagram is next.

questiontext.text:
Read the Airworthiness Directive note.

Airworthiness Directive AD-2026-11 is mandatory. It requires a one-time inspection of the cabin door hinge for cracks within 300 flight hours. Non-compliance makes the aircraft unairworthy.

What is true of this Airworthiness Directive?

generalfeedback.text: An Airworthiness Directive is mandatory. Unlike a recommended Service Bulletin, non-compliance makes the aircraft unairworthy.

feedback.text: Correct — an AD is compulsory; non-compliance grounds the aircraft.
A recommendation would be a Service Bulletin, not an AD.

answer.text: It applies to the engine only

feedback.text: This AD is about the cabin door hinge.

questiontext.text:
Write one linking word that shows a result:

"The seal was worn. ______, we replaced it."

generalfeedback.text: A result connector fits: Therefore / So / Consequently. The replacement follows from the worn seal.

feedback.text: Correct — "Therefore" marks the result.
Correct — "So" also shows the result.
Correct — "Consequently" shows the result.

questiontext.text:
Write one linking word that gives the reason:

"We removed the valve ______ it was leaking."

generalfeedback.text: A reason connector introduces the cause: because / since / as.

feedback.text: Correct — "because" introduces the reason.
Correct — "since" can mean "because" here.
Correct — "as" can give the reason.

questiontext.text:
This sentence has two linking words for one join: "Because the seal was worn, so we replaced it."

Type only the one word you delete to correct it.

generalfeedback.text: English uses one linking word per join. "Because" already links the cause, so delete "so".

feedback.text: Correct — delete "so"; "Because…" is enough.

questiontext.text:
Write the one word that fits before a clause:

"The flight was delayed ______ the seal was worn." (not "because of")

generalfeedback.text: "because of" takes a noun; before a clause use "because" (also "since" or "as").

feedback.text: Correct — "because" + clause.
Accepted — "since" also introduces the clause.
Accepted — "as" also introduces the clause.

name.text: U20-U5 Bank term — one tracked item

questiontext.text:
Complete the term (two words):

"The unique code for one single tracked item is the ______ ______."

generalfeedback.text: A serial number identifies one single item, and no other. A batch number, by contrast, covers a whole group.

feedback.text: Correct — the serial number identifies one single item.

questiontext.text:
Complete the term (one word):

"A second qualified person confirms safety-critical work in a ______ inspection."

generalfeedback.text: A dual inspection is the second, independent check of safety-critical work.

feedback.text: Correct — a dual inspection.

name.text: U20-U7 Linking word — reason at the batch step

questiontext.text:
Write one linking word giving the reason:

"Record the batch number ______ the seal has no serial number."

generalfeedback.text: This is a reason join: since / because / as. In the dialogue the mentor uses "since".

feedback.text: Correct — "since" gives the reason (as in the dialogue).
Correct — "because" gives the reason.
Correct — "as" can give the reason.

name.text: U20-V1 Match term to plain meaning

questiontext.text: Match each documentation-trail term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: Documentation trail = the whole linked set; traceability = following it start to end; cross-reference = the link between documents; audit trail = what an auditor follows; rectification = the completed repair; corrective action = the exact work done.

answer.text: the full set of linked records for one defect
being able to follow a job from start to finish
a link from one document to a place in another
the linked record an auditor follows to check work
the completed repair that clears the defect
the exact work carried out to fix the defect

name.text: U20-V2 Match term to its verb (collocation)

questiontext.text: Match each term to the verb it goes with in a maintenance record.

generalfeedback.text: raise a work order · quote the part number · carry out a dual inspection · note the batch number · sign the sign-off block. Learning the verb helps you write the record correctly.

questiontext.text: Choose the correct verb: "You ______ a work order to open the job."

generalfeedback.text: The fixed collocation is "raise a work order". You raise it to open and authorise the job.

feedback.text: Correct — you raise a work order.
Not the maintenance collocation.
We do not "publish" a work order.

questiontext.text: Choose the correct verb: "When there is no serial number, ______ the batch number on the record."

generalfeedback.text: The collocation is "note the batch number" (also "record the batch number"). You write it down for traceability.

feedback.text: Correct — note (record) the batch number.
Ignoring it would break traceability.
You keep the batch number, not delete it.
